summary: The milestone completed 12 experiments in 2.9 minutes, and 4 were compute-bound. The adapter-readiness benchmark led compute time, followed by the matched live-agent canary; adapter readiness is the only stated constraint, and no cause is available for the canary duration. The locked task-level classification reports no GPU idle on compute-bound work, while the available data does not explain multi-model dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Adapter-readiness gating is the only stated constraint on the longest compute-bound entry; the data does not separate gate wait from compute time.
Disk modification-time reconstruction does not isolate gate wait, launch, model load, inference, verification, or artifact-write time.
The GPU snapshot is not joined to an active experiment, process, loaded-model count, or dispatcher choice, so it cannot establish task-time utilization or DualGPURunner selection.
improvements_suggested: Add an adapter-readiness preflight and cache its receipt before the gated exact-state benchmark starts.
Emit monotonic phase timings for gate wait, launch, model load, inference, verification, and artifact writing.
Join GPU samples to experiment identity, process identity, active phase, loaded-model count, and dispatcher choice.
Select DualGPURunner only when telemetry confirms that at least two models are loaded concurrently, and record the selection receipt.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Preflight adapter readiness and reuse a valid readiness receipt.
Replace disk-time reconstruction with monotonic per-phase timing.
Record task-linked GPU, model-count, and runner-selection telemetry.
meta_reflection: The timing ledger orders the work but does not support causal diagnosis. The GPU snapshot shows idle devices, but the locked task-level field is false and no concurrent-model evidence is supplied, so stronger utilization and runner claims would be unsupported.
